We find a potential negative correlation between $T_{\rm dust}$ and gas-phase metallicity with $T_{\rm dust}\propto Z^{-0.50\pm0.19}$, implying decreased dust shielding and efficient dust heating in low-metallicity environments. Given the systematic offset of $T_{\rm dust}$ between $z\sim0$ and $z\sim6-9$ at fixed metallicity, we find $T_{\rm dust}$ is well described by sSFR as well as $Z$ with $\log T_{\rm dust}=-0.25^{+0.03}_{-0.04}\times(\log Z-0.57\times\log {\rm sSFR})+4.88^{+0.47}_{-0.43}$ across $z\sim0$ to $z\sim6-9$. Simultaneously with the dust continuum, these observations cover the [OI]63$μ$m emission line for five galaxies, which traces dense neutral gas. We find a lower [CII]/[OI] ratio in $z\gtrsim6$ galaxies than in local samples, suggesting that [CII] becomes fainter due to collisional de-excitation at high gas density. Combining the [OI], [OIII], and [CII] lines and cloudy modeling, our results imply $\log U_{\rm ion}\sim-2$ and $\log n_{\rm H}\,[{\rm cm}^{-3}]\sim2.5$ in $z\gtrsim6$ galaxies, which is $\sim3-10\times$ higher $U_{\rm ion}$ and $\sim2-3\times$ higher $n_{\rm H}$ than the local samples. The combination of these enhanced $U_{\rm ion}$ and $n_{\rm H}$ naturally explains the high [OIII]/[CII] ratio at $z\gtrsim6$.

AI.tldr: This paper presents ALMA high-frequency observations of nine bright Lyman-break galaxies at z~6-8.3, measuring dust temperatures and finding most galaxies show T_dust~40K while three show higher values. They find a negative correlation between dust temperature and metallicity, and develop a relation linking T_dust to specific star formation rate and metallicity across cosmic time. They also analyze [OI]63μm, [CII], and [OIII] line ratios to infer gas properties, finding enhanced ionization parameters and gas densities in z>6 galaxies compared to local samples.
AI.motivation: To better constrain the dust temperature in a statistical sample of z>6 galaxies using new ALMA Band-9 and/or 10 observations, enabling studies of dust properties in the early universe and understanding the physical conditions of star-forming galaxies at high redshift.
AI.method: Analysis of ALMA high-frequency (Band-9/10) observations of nine bright Lyman-break galaxies at 5.8<z<8.3, with five newly observed galaxies at z~6. Dust continuum measurements constrain T_dust; spectral line analysis of [OI]63μm, [CII], [OIII] combined with cloudy radiative transfer modeling to derive ionization parameters and gas densities.
AI.result: Most z~6-9 star-forming galaxies show T_dust~40K on average, while three show T_dust>60K. A negative correlation T_dust∝Z^-0.50±0.19 is found. T_dust is described by log T_dust=-0.25×(log Z-0.57×log sSFR)+4.88 across z~0 to z~6-9. Lower [CII]/[OI] ratios in z>6 galaxies suggest collisional de-excitation at high gas density. Modeling implies log U_ion~-2 and log n_H~2.5 cm^-3, which are 3-10x higher in U_ion and 2-3x higher in n_H than local samples, explaining the high [OIII]/[CII] ratio at z>6.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced dust heating in low-metallicity environments and systematically higher T_dust at fixed metallicity for high-z galaxies suggest different ISM conditions in the early universe. The elevated U_ion and n_H derived from multi-line observations naturally explain the high [OIII]/[CII] ratio characteristic of z>6 galaxies, providing a coherent physical picture of the ISM conditions in early star-forming galaxies.

title: Near universality of nonlinear transverse and radial velocity responses in spherical collapse with arbitrary radial profiles
summary: The nonlinear relation between density and expansion is usually formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat, which has a single local Hubble rate. A smooth spherical profile instead expands differently along ($H_{\parallel}$) and across ($H_{\perp}$) the radial direction-a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. We show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise response is nevertheless fixed by one top-hat function. Given the local density contrast $δ(t,r)$ and the enclosed contrast $Δ(t,r)$, a transverse response and its derivative determine $H_{\perp}$ and $H_{\parallel}$. The linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the usual growth rate $f$. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation. We check that it reconstructs full $Λ$LTB profiles to numerical precision. We also provide a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit that requires only $f$, $δ$, and $Δ$. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell located in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are $0.3\%$ and $0.7\%$ in the transverse and radial responses, respectively. This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response and makes the effect of radial gradients explicit.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise expansion response of a smooth spherical density profile (radial and transverse Hubble rates) is fixed by a single top-hat function. Given the local and enclosed density contrasts, the linear and second-order limits are simple algebraic maps involving only the growth rate f, and an exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating evolution equations. A derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit achieves maximum relative errors of 0.3% and 0.7% in transverse and radial responses across representative matter-curvature-redshift combinations.
AI.motivation: The standard relation between density and expansion assumes a homogeneous spherical top hat with a single Hubble rate, but smooth spherical density profiles expand anisotropically (differently along and across the radial direction). The authors aim to formulate a compact, exact, and cosmology-independent map between the density profile and its anisotropic expansion response, separating profile production from expansion response and making radial gradient effects explicit.
AI.method: The authors establish that the transverse response and its derivative determine H_parallel and H_perpendicular. They derive linear and second-order algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the growth rate f, and construct an exact equal-age nonlinear response that avoids integrating evolution equations. They verify the construction against full LambdaLTB profiles and provide a derivative-aware three-term symbolic fit requiring only f, local density contrast delta, and enclosed contrast Delta.
AI.result: The exact equal-age construction reconstructs full LambdaLTB profiles to numerical precision. The symbolic fit achieves maximum relative errors of 0.3% in the transverse response and 0.7% in the radial response across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations for a shell in the compensated transition region.
AI.conclusion: The complete shellwise expansion response of a radially inhomogeneous spherical profile is fixed by a single top-hat function for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant. The compact formulation decouples density profile production from expansion response and explicitly exposes the effect of radial gradients, providing a practical tool without costly evolution integrations.

title: The solitary star cluster of the Andromeda XXV dwarf spheroidal
comment: Resubmitted to MNRAS after a positive referee report. 11 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables
summary: We present Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys observations of Gep I, a globular cluster (GC) candidate in the low-mass ($M_{\star}\sim 6.5 \times 10^5\,M_{\odot}$) M31 dwarf spheroidal (dSph) satellite Andromeda XXV (And XXV). We confirm the nature of this object and provide the first detailed characterisation of its resolved stellar populations using a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) that reaches 2 magnitudes below the horizontal branch. We compare Gep I's metallicity and distance with those of the surrounding And XXV stellar population, and find them to be strikingly similar, consistent with a physical association between the GC and the dSph. Gep I is very extended ($R_h=24^{+5}_{-4}$ pc) and faint ($M_V = -4.5 \pm 0.2$ mag), similar to the star clusters residing in other low-mass dwarf galaxies. It is characterised by a very low metallicity ($\rm [Fe/H] = -2.4^{+0.3}_{-0.4}\,$dex) and a red horizontal branch morphology, a combination also seen in suspected accreted GCs in the M31 halo and in the Local Group dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 6822. While Gep I is most likely a genuine star cluster, the current data do not exclude the tantalising possibility that it consists of And XXV stars temporarily captured by a dark subhalo orbiting within the dSph's potential well.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Hubble Space Telescope observations confirming Gep I as a globular cluster candidate in the low-mass M31 dwarf spheroidal galaxy Andromeda XXV, characterising it as an extended, faint, very metal-poor cluster with a red horizontal branch that is physically associated with its host dSph.
AI.motivation: To confirm the nature of Gep I, a globular cluster candidate in the low-mass dwarf spheroidal galaxy And XXV, and provide the first detailed characterisation of its resolved stellar populations, while comparing its properties to the surrounding dSph stellar population to assess their physical association.
AI.method: The study uses Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys observations to construct a colour-magnitude diagram reaching 2 magnitudes below the horizontal branch, comparing the metallicity and distance of Gep I with the surrounding And XXV stellar population, and characterising its structural and photometric properties.
AI.result: Gep I is confirmed as an extended (R_h = 24 pc) and faint (M_V = -4.5 mag) cluster with very low metallicity ([Fe/H] = -2.4 dex) and a red horizontal branch morphology. Its metallicity and distance are strikingly similar to those of the surrounding And XXV population, consistent with physical association, and its properties resemble star clusters in other low-mass dwarf galaxies and suspected accreted GCs in the M31 halo.
AI.conclusion: Gep I is most likely a genuine star cluster physically associated with And XXV, though the current data do not exclude the possibility that it consists of And XXV stars temporarily captured by a dark subhalo orbiting within the dSph's potential well.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Constraints on the anisotropic screening and birefringence effects with DR6
comment: 31 pages, 24 figures. To be submitted to ApJ
summary: While we have learned much from recent surveys of the mm-wave sky, many secondary anisotropies of the CMB remain under-explored. We consider two of these here: the anisotropic screening induced by Thomson scattering of CMB photons off free electrons, and cosmic birefringence, the rotation of CMB polarization due to parity-violating physics beyond the standard model. To measure these effects, we apply state-of-the-art estimators for statistical anisotropy to the ACT Data Release 6 CMB data and construct noisy maps and power spectra of both effects. For anisotropic screening, we find no significant detection with the baseline data, and place an upper limit on its power spectrum that is two orders of magnitude above predictions from current reionization models. We obtain evidence for some foreground contamination at one of our frequencies that is consistent with expectations from extragalactic simulations. For our anisotropic birefringence analysis, we also find no detection and place an upper limit on the signal that is consistent with previous analyses. We report a corresponding upper limit on the Chern-Simons coupling term $g_{a γ} < 4.9 \times 10^{-2} / H_\mathrm{I}$, with $H_\mathrm{I}$ the inflationary Hubble scale. These analyses pave the way toward obtaining improved constraints with the next generation of ground-based CMB surveys.

AI.tldr: The paper applies state-of-the-art statistical anisotropy estimators to ACT Data Release 6 CMB data to probe two underexplored secondary CMB anisotropies: anisotropic screening (from Thomson scattering off free electrons) and anisotropic cosmic birefringence (parity-violating polarization rotation). No significant detections are found for either effect; upper limits are placed on their power spectra, including a constraint on the Chern-Simons coupling g_aγ < 4.9×10⁻²/H_I, consistent with previous analyses and paving the way for future ground-based CMB surveys.
AI.motivation: While recent mm-wave CMB surveys have been extensively used to study primary anisotropies, several secondary CMB anisotropies remain underexplored. This work aims to probe two such effects—anisotropic screening from Thomson scattering and cosmic birefringence from parity-violating new physics—using high-quality ACT DR6 observations.
AI.method: The authors apply state-of-the-art estimators for statistical anisotropy to ACT Data Release 6 CMB data and construct (noisy) maps and power spectra for both anisotropic screening and anisotropic cosmic birefringence effects.
AI.result: No significant detection of anisotropic screening; upper limit on its power spectrum is two orders of magnitude above reionization model predictions. Some foreground contamination at one frequency consistent with extragalactic simulations. No detection of anisotropic birefringence; upper limit consistent with previous analyses; Chern-Simons coupling constrained to g_aγ < 4.9×10⁻²/H_I.
AI.conclusion: These analyses set the first dedicated ACT DR6 constraints on both secondary effects and demonstrate a viable pathway toward significantly improved constraints with the next generation of ground-based CMB surveys.

title: HURACAN: A comparison of stellar and interstellar proper motions inside L1688
comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables, submitted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The assumption that molecular clouds are kinematically coupled to the young stellar populations forming within them is observationally still poorly constrained. With the transverse component $v_{\textrm{t}}$ of the interstellar medium (ISM) motion being largely unknown, the three-dimensional kinematic state of even the closest clouds remains incomplete. We provide the first direct measurement of the transverse motion of the ISM inside the Ophiuchus cloud L1688 and compare it with the kinematics of the surrounding young stellar populations. The measurement was obtained using intensity-based image registration applied to archival data, allowing us to generate a proper motion field of the studied regions and determine the cloud's bulk motion, $(μ_{α^*},μ_δ)^{\mathrm{ISM}}_{\mathrm{median}}=(-3.0, -24.1)$ mas yr$^{-1}$. This motion differs from the kinematics of the youngest population in Upper Scorpius by $3\pm1$ km s$^{-1}$, highlighting the possibility of a bias when using stars as a proxy for the ISM motion near star-forming regions. By comparing the cloud's motion with that of the youngest stellar population in the region and the B-star Oph S1 located within the cloud, we find that stellar feedback must have dynamically shaped the motion of the ISM over the last few million years. Furthermore, by studying a shell-like ISM structure appearing in L1688, we find evidence suggesting that this object is likely neither a typical Herbig-Haro object nor a supernova remnant, with its origin remaining a mystery. Our results demonstrate that archival and future high-resolution near-infrared observations can and will continue to enable measurements of ISM transverse motions in nearby clouds, opening a new window for studying ISM dynamics that is not accessible when using radial velocities alone.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first direct measurement of the transverse motion of the interstellar medium (ISM) inside the Ophiuchus cloud L1688, obtaining a median proper motion of (−3.0, −24.1) mas yr⁻¹ using intensity-based image registration on archival data. The ISM motion differs from the youngest stellar population in Upper Scorpius by 3±1 km s⁻¹, suggesting potential bias when using stars as proxies for ISM motion. The comparison with stellar populations and the B-star Oph S1 indicates stellar feedback shaped the ISM over the last few million years. The study also identifies a shell-like structure likely neither a Herbig-Haro object nor a supernova remnant, with unknown origin.
AI.motivation: The three-dimensional kinematic state of molecular clouds remains incomplete because the transverse component of ISM motion is largely unknown; this paper aims to directly measure transverse ISM motion and compare it with young stellar kinematics to constrain the assumption that clouds and their forming stars are kinematically coupled.
AI.method: The authors applied intensity-based image registration to archival high-resolution near-infrared data to generate a proper motion field of the Ophiuchus cloud L1688, determining the cloud's bulk transverse motion and comparing it with the kinematics of surrounding young stellar populations.
AI.result: The cloud's bulk ISM motion is measured as (μ_α*, μ_δ)_median = (−3.0, −24.1) mas yr⁻¹, differing from the youngest Upper Scorpius stellar population by 3±1 km s⁻¹. Stellar feedback from the youngest stars and Oph S1 appears to have dynamically shaped the ISM. A shell-like ISM structure was found to be neither a typical Herbig-Haro object nor a supernova remnant, with its origin remaining a mystery.
AI.conclusion: Archival and future high-resolution near-infrared observations can enable measurements of ISM transverse motions in nearby clouds, opening a new window for studying ISM dynamics that is inaccessible through radial velocities alone, and highlighting potential biases in using stars as proxies for ISM motion.

title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
comment: Submitted to MNRAS. 18 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables
summary: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of $\sim$0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on shallow, low-resolution photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 132 spectra of red giant and horizontal branch stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure $\rm [Fe/H] =-0.61\pm0.03\,$dex, $v_{\rm los} = 50.9^{+0.8}_{-0.7}\,\rm km \,s^{-1}$, $σ_v = 3.2^{+1.4}_{-1.5}\,\rm km \,s^{-1}$. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a $\sim$3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius ($R_{h}=8.8^{+1.1}_{-1.3}\,$pc), a small flattening ($e=0.14^{+0.12}_{-0.10}$), and low luminosity ($M_{V} = -5.0 \pm 0.4$). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique GC system.

AI.tldr: The paper reinvestigates Fornax 6, a previously identified overdensity in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy, using MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations and deep GMOS-S imagery. With 132 spectra, the authors confirm Fornax 6 as a genuine globular cluster with 43 likely members, measuring [Fe/H] = -0.61 ± 0.03 dex, v_los = 50.9 km/s, σ_v = 3.2 km/s, and an age of ~3 Gyr (derived from the first observed main-sequence turn-off). The cluster has an irregular morphology, a half-light radius of ~8.8 pc, small flattening, and low luminosity (M_V = -5.0 ± 0.4), making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's GC system, likely undergoing tidal disruption.
AI.motivation: To definitively determine whether Fornax 6 is a genuine globular cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy, since prior classification was based on shallow, low-resolution photometry and limited spectroscopy, while GCs in Fornax are important tracers of dark matter properties.
AI.method: Analysis of MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode integral-field spectroscopy combined with deep GMOS-S imaging. Extraction of 132 spectra of red giant and horizontal branch stars for chemo-dynamical analysis, identification of cluster members via kinematics and chemistry, and fitting of isochrones and structural parameters.
AI.result: Fornax 6 is confirmed as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with 43 likely members. Its properties are [Fe/H] = -0.61 ± 0.03 dex, v_los = 50.9 km/s, σ_v = 3.2 km/s, age ~3 Gyr (from the first-ever observed main-sequence turn-off), half-light radius 8.8 pc, flattening e = 0.14, and M_V = -5.0 ± 0.4. It shows an irregular morphology consistent with tidal disruption and is the youngest and most metal-rich globular cluster in Fornax.
AI.conclusion: Fornax 6 is a genuine low-mass globular cluster that is likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's globular cluster system. This improved characterization has implications for understanding the formation and dynamical evolution of globular clusters in dwarf galaxies and for using them as dark matter tracers.

title: Exploring the survivability of higher-order multiple protostellar systems -- The case of VLA1623
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS (Accepted 2026 August 27. Received 2026 August 27; in original form 2025 December 17)
summary: Higher-order protostellar systems ($\geq$3 components) are commonly observed in the early stages of low-mass star formation. A persistent question in star formation and evolution is whether these higher-order protostellar systems survive as gravitationally bound systems or dissolve into binaries over time. We explore this question with a case study of the embedded quadruple protostellar system VLA1623 and its observational constraints, assuming that the components A1, A2, B, and W are gravitationally bound. Using $N$-body simulations, we run a grid of models considering gravity, mass accretion onto protostars, the presence of the protostellar cloud core, and its dispersal. The simulations are integrated over a period of 8 Myr to take into account the evolution from the protostellar phase (Class 0 and I, 1 Myr), through the pre-main sequence (Class II and III, 2 -- 3 Myr), and into the main sequence (4 Myr). Our results show that VLA1623 has a probability of 30% to remain as a gravitationally-bound quadruple system up to 8 Myr from the current state. There is also a 25--30% probability of VLA1623 dissolving into a triple system. This suggests that the dissolution of quadruple protostellar systems contributes to the formation of stable triple (proto)stellar systems. Components A1 and A2 are the most likely to be ejected, while W has a lower probability of being ejected from the system. The stability of VLA1623 depends on a combination of component mass ratios wrt the primary, separations, and eccentricities.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether higher-order protostellar systems survive as gravitationally bound systems or dissolve into binaries, using VLA1623—an embedded quadruple protostellar system—as a case study. N-body simulations over 8 Myr show a 30% probability of remaining a bound quadruple system and a 25–30% probability of dissolving into a triple, suggesting that quadruple systems can contribute to the formation of stable triple systems.
AI.motivation: Higher-order protostellar systems (≥3 components) are common in early low-mass star formation, but it is unclear whether these systems persist as bound multiples or dissolve into binaries over time. Understanding this fate is important for the overall picture of star formation and evolution.
AI.method: The authors performed N-body simulations of the VLA1623 quadruple protostellar system, running a grid of models that include gravity, mass accretion onto protostars, the presence of the protostellar cloud core, and core dispersal. Simulations were integrated over 8 Myr, covering the protostellar phase (Class 0/I), pre-main sequence (Class II/III), and main sequence phases.
AI.result: VLA1623 has a 30% probability of remaining a gravitationally-bound quadruple system over 8 Myr and a 25–30% probability of dissolving into a triple system. Components A1 and A2 are the most likely to be ejected, while W is less likely to be ejected. System stability depends on the combination of component mass ratios, separations, and eccentricities.
AI.conclusion: The dissolution of quadruple protostellar systems can contribute to the formation of stable triple (proto)stellar systems, providing insight into the dynamical evolution and ultimate fate of higher-order protostellar systems.

title: $N$-body simulations of the open cluster population in the Milky Way and the impact of GMC encounters
summary: We investigate the population of open clusters in the Solar Neighbourhood and model the effect of encounters with giant molecular clouds (GMCs) over the last 1 Gyr. We combine a Galactic model with $N$-body simulations of 20692 unique clusters in the mass range $[50-24000]$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$. Each cluster is simulated twice: with and without tidal forces from the GMCs. We find that an initial cluster mass function truncated at $\sim 9000$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ best reproduces the observed mass function evolution. For the age function, the observations show a decline in clusters for ages older than $\sim 1$ Myr, whereas our simulated clusters show a decline after $\sim 50$ Myr. The observed early disruption suggests that some clusters form supervirial, whereas our simulated clusters are created in virial equilibrium. Low-mass ($<600 \, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters are most sensitive to GMC encounters, which accelerate their disruption in the first $\sim 200$ Myr. After $\sim 500$ Myr, the impact of GMCs becomes irrelevant since the clusters will have been destroyed regardless of whether they experience GMC encounters or not. The survival of intermediate-mass ($600-6000\, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters is significantly reduced by GMCs at ages up to 1 Gyr. High-mass ($>6000 \, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) clusters survive to 1 Gyr with minimal disruption with or without GMCs. We find that clusters that have had strong GMC encounters within the last $20$ Myr should have tidal tails that are randomly orientated with respect to the Galactic centre.

AI.tldr: This paper combines a Galactic model with N-body simulations of 20,692 open clusters (50–24,000 M☉) to study how GMC encounters affect cluster populations in the Solar Neighbourhood over 1 Gyr. Key findings: an initial cluster mass function truncated at ~9000 M☉ best matches observations; observed clusters disrupt faster (~1 Myr) than simulated ones (~50 Myr), suggesting supervirial cluster formation; low-mass clusters are most GMC-sensitive in the first ~200 Myr, while GMC effects become negligible after ~500 Myr; intermediate-mass clusters (600–6000 M☉) are significantly affected up to 1 Gyr; high-mass clusters survive largely unaffected; and recently disrupted clusters show randomly orientated tidal tails relative to the Galactic centre.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of giant molecular cloud encounters in the disruption and evolution of open clusters in the Solar Neighbourhood, and to explain discrepancies between observed and simulated cluster mass and age functions.
AI.method: The authors combine a Galactic model with N-body simulations of 20,692 unique clusters spanning masses 50–24,000 M☉. Each cluster is simulated twice—once with and once without tidal forces from GMCs—to isolate the effect of GMC encounters on cluster evolution over the last 1 Gyr.
AI.result: An initial cluster mass function truncated at ~9000 M☉ best reproduces observed mass function evolution. Simulated clusters show age decline after ~50 Myr versus ~1 Myr observed, indicating supervirial formation in nature. Low-mass (<600 M☉) clusters are most GMC-sensitive within ~200 Myr; GMC effects become negligible after ~500 Myr. Intermediate-mass (600–6000 M☉) cluster survival is significantly reduced by GMCs up to 1 Gyr. High-mass (>6000 M☉) clusters survive to 1 Gyr with minimal disruption either way. Clusters with strong GMC encounters within the last 20 Myr have randomly orientated tidal tails relative to the Galactic centre.
AI.conclusion: GMC encounters play a significant role in disrupting low- and intermediate-mass open clusters, but their influence diminishes with cluster mass and age. The discrepancy in disruption timescales between observed and simulated clusters suggests clusters form supervirial, not in virial equilibrium. The observable signature of recent strong GMC encounters is randomly orientated tidal tails with respect to the Galactic centre.

title: Non-isothermal vertical distribution functions for the Milky Way
summary: The vertical structure of our Galaxy has commonly been assumed to follow a pseudo-isothermal distribution. However, there is no \textit{a priori} reason to expect this form to arise from scattering by giant molecular clouds (GMCs), since GMCs are confined to a narrow layer around the Galactic midplane and therefore do not randomise stars uniformly in vertical phase space. We first present a simple statistical argument to derive a new vertical distribution function (DF), in the limiting case of a razor-thin distribution of GMCs, which admits an extra factor of ${J_z}^{-α}$, where $α>0$ and varies for different potentials. In light of this, we revisit the diffusion coefficients for vertical heating from the mechanics of two-body scattering, in a more realistic, extended distribution of GMCs. The resulting drift and diffusion coefficients are strongly non-linear in $v_z$, particularly at low relative velocities, where the effective range of weak, local encounters can vanish. We determine stationary solutions, and also numerically solve the orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation with time-dependent coefficients. We find, in both cases, a vertical action distribution that deviates from that of the pseudo-isothermal case, and propose a new, family of vertical DFs that generalise the pseudo-isothermal form. We find the two primary agents of non-isothermality are: (i) a GMC distribution confined near the midplane, and (ii) the fact that the Coulomb logarithm, $Λ$ is strongly velocity-dependent at small velocities, and cannot be treated as a constant, contrary to the commonly adopted assumption.

Through statistical arguments, diffusion coefficient analysis, and numerical Fokker-Planck solutions, the authors identify two causes of non-isothermality: the confined GMC distribution and the strongly velocity-dependent Coulomb logarithm.

The two primary causes of non-isothermality are identified: (i) the GMC distribution confined near the midplane, and (ii) the velocity-dependent Coulomb logarithm Λ, which cannot be treated as constant especially at small velocities.

title: LightCube: A Parsec-Resolution 3D Model of the Local Far-Ultraviolet Interstellar Radiation Field
summary: We present a three-dimensional model of the local interstellar radiation field (ISRF) in the ultraviolet (UV). Using UV flux measurements from the TD1 catalog and stellar distances from Gaia and Hipparcos, we construct a catalog of stars that we expect to dominate the UV flux in the nearby Galaxy. We use the radiative transfer code DIRTY to model the propagation of photons from these stars through a 3D dust map, including the effects of scattering and absorption. The result is LightCube, a model of the ultraviolet ISRF out to 1.25 kpc from the Sun, with a maximum linear resolution of 1 pc. We model the ISRF in the four TD1 bands (1565 A, 1965 A, 2365 A, and 2740 A), as well as a single value for the full FUV range, and calculate the ISRF at the Sun to be 5.65$\times$10$^{-14}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ from 912 A to 2000 A. The modeled ISRF is quite variable, with more than an order of magnitude variation seen in dense regions, and about half that in lower density regions. By comparing LightCube to an estimate of the 3D distribution of total-to-selective extinction ratio, $R_V$, we find a positive correlation between UV flux and $R_V$ in regions of low UV radiation.

The model covers four TD1 UV bands and the full FUV range, finding the ISRF at the Sun to be 5.65×10⁻¹⁴ erg cm⁻³ (912–2000 Å), with more than an order of magnitude variation in dense regions and a positive correlation between UV flux and the dust extinction ratio R_V in low-radiation regions.

They then use the DIRTY radiative transfer code to propagate photons from these stars through a 3D dust map, accounting for both scattering and absorption, to produce LightCube at up to 1 pc linear resolution.

The modeled ISRF varies by over an order of magnitude in dense regions and about half that in lower-density regions. title: Map of the Interstellar Continuum FUV Field within 800 Parsecs
summary: The far-ultraviolet (FUV) field, consisting of photons with energies between 6 and 13.6 electron volts, plays an important role in the chemical and thermodynamical evolution of the interstellar medium. FUV continuum radiation is produced by bright stars in the galaxy and absorbed by interstellar dust. We used newly available maps of the dust distribution, in conjunction with catalogs of stellar positions and spectra, to create a map of the stellar FUV field within 800 parsecs of the Earth. The map shows a total FUV intensity in the solar neighborhood in line with existing measurements (0.7 times the Draine field), but substantial point-to-point fluctuations exist. Near the Galactic midplane, the FUV intensity decreases with increasing gas density up to a density of approximately 10 hydrogen atoms per cm$^3$, due to absorption of light by dust. Between 10 and 50 hydrogen atoms per cm$^3$ the UV field increases again, due to a positive correlation between high density gas and young hot stars. We find that the spectrum is generally harder where the UV field is higher, and softer in regions where dust extinction is more important. The resulting map, as well as our catalog of derived stellar properties, are both available for download for those wishing to study a nearby region of the ISM.

The map shows a total FUV intensity of 0.7 times the Draine field, with significant point-to-point fluctuations, and reveals a non-monotonic relationship between FUV intensity and gas density due to competing effects of dust absorption and association with young hot stars. The map and catalog of stellar properties are made publicly available.
